children: is preparing to build a new hybrid vehicle factory in Ohio that could require an investment of as much as $2.5 billion, Nikkei reported on Thursday, as the automaker approaches the limits of its existing North American production capacity.

The Japanese automaker is considering spending 300 billion yen to 400 billion yen ($1.9 billion to $2.5 billion) on the facility, with production potentially beginning in 2030, according to the report.
US spokesman said no decision has been made on a new plant.
The company’s plans come as uncertainty over the future of the US-Mexico-Canada trade agreement weighs on investment decisions. Honda
Executive Vice President Noriya Kaihara said last month that the automaker may need another North American assembly plant but could change course if the trade pact is not extended.
has said it would need to make a decision within the next one to two years, with the aim of having any new facility operational around 2030.

The automaker has already put an $11 billion Canadian electric-vehicle and battery project on hold indefinitely and canceled three planned EVs for the US market. Last year, it also shifted production of its US-bound five-door Civic hybrid from Japan to Indiana.

title: Honda weighs $2.5B Ohio hybrid plant as US capacity tightens
